summary: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive educational simulator developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, designed for children aged 7 to 13 to command a 10-Sol space voyage. The project combines the management of vital resources (oxygen and energy) with real-time scientific alerts based on the NASA DONKI database (covering space weather and CMEs). Built using React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, it integrates a dynamic time system and space protocols to introduce space science to the next generation in a way that is both engaging and scientifically rigorous.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive web-based space simulation designed for children aged 7 to 13. Players command a 10-Sol deep-space mission where they must monitor and manage vital resources like Oxygen and Energy in real-time, while reacting to simulated space weather emergencies and cosmic challenges.

The project fosters early interest in STEM. Its primary impact is to educate the next generation of space explorers on real-world space survival, resource management, and space weather awareness.

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS for a fully responsive, immersive space interface and custom animations.
  • Audio: Web Audio API for generating native spatial alarm effects.
  • Data Sources: Official NASA DONKI API integration for real-time Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) and solar storm alert dynamics.
  • Deployment: Hosted live on Vercel https://junior-astronaut-trainer.vercel.app/)

The project creatively bridges complex scientific data (NASA DONKI) with child-friendly storytelling and gamification. Our team carefully considered accessibility, age-appropriate UI/UX design (intuitive buttons for recycling and repairs), and balancing educational value with immersive entertainment to keep young learners engaged throughout the 10-Sol journey.
